Subject: Inference deployment economics — hosted vs dedicated vs private (recap + asks)

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so the team can run a tailored TCO: 

Summary of BrightLeaf constraints / goals
- Peak latency target: p95 < 120ms for customer-facing recommendations.
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~55 requests/sec; burst up to ~180 rps for 10–20 min during batch windows.
- Typical prompt: 1.1k input tokens, 350 output tokens.
- Data residency: US-only for now; potential PHI-scope on a subset of customers (likely needs VPC/KMS).
- Pilot timeline: 6–8 weeks; production rollout by Q4.

High-level deployment options we discussed
1) Hosted API (fastest pilot): pay-as-you-go per-token pricing; minimal infra ops; good for bootstrapping but unit cost is higher at scale.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput, lower per-token cost for sustained volume; requires commit (monthly or annual). Good middle ground if BrightLeaf wants predictable performance.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation and control, KMS/HSM support, on-prem possible for PHI — higher upfront work and platform fee.

Initial cost modeling asks (what we need from you)
- Representative usage CSV with timestamped request sizes (input/output tokens) and peak week/day indicators (attached sample format).
- Procurement constraints: preferred billing cadence (monthly/annual) and any required contract language (term limits, SLAs).

What Redwood will deliver next
- A two-scenario TCO spreadsheet (pilot: hosted path; production: dedicated reserved commit) with line-items for per-token vs capacity economics, expected monthly spend, and break-even point.
- Security checklist items for Private/VPC if PHI is in-scope.

Attachments: BrightLeaf_usage_sample_q3.csv (format we prefer), Redwood_prelim_cost_models.xlsx (stub with example rows).

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up on Wednesday 24 Aug to walk the usage file and validate assumptions. If that works, send a calendar invite with ops/procurement included.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the upload. I pulled the sample and started a quick baseline. Attached is a preliminary workbook (Redwood_prelim_cost_models.xlsx) with three scenario tabs: pilot-hosted, dedicated-12mo-commit, and private-vpc-upfront. Key assumptions called out in tab headers.

Quick highlights from baseline (very top-line; we'll refine on Wed)
- Pilot (hosted): estimated $12.6k/month at current token run-rate (includes caching and a modest 7% sampling for streaming overhead). Pros: fast start, no commit. Cons: per-token spend increases with traffic.
- Dedicated (12-mo reserved): estimated $8.9k/month equivalent when amortized (includes reserved capacity + managed overhead). Break-even vs hosted at ~1.6M tokens/day under our model. Pros: lower unit cost at scale, predictable latency.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time onboarding/infra bundling estimated ~$120k–$180k (depending on on-prem vs hosted VPC variant) + ~$6k/mo recurring platform fee. Pros: full control, KMS/HSM, PHI-compliant.

Caveats
- These numbers assume model parity (same model family) and vanilla quantization. If BrightLeaf requires more aggressive quantization or custom kernels, costs shift.
- We will run a sensitivity analysis on prompt length, cache hit rate (we used 18% prefix caching), and commit term (12 vs 24 months) on Wednesday.

Next steps
1) Wed 24 Aug, 10:00am PT call to walk the spreadsheet (I sent a calendar invite).
2) Post-call: Redwood will provide a two-scenario TCO (pdf + spreadsheet) oriented to procurement language and a draft SOW for Private if requested.

Forwarding the preview workbook here. If procurement has strict billing cadence requirements, flag them on the Wed call so we model accurate commit discounts.

Best — Diego
Diego Fernandez

Diego / Steph — quick internal note before Wed:

Internal pricing guidance (do not share externally)
- For a deal size that looks like BrightLeaf (steady ~1.1M–2.5M tokens/day): target offering is Dedicated with a 12–24 month commit. Recommend 15% list discount off published dedicated rates for a 12mo commit, 23% for 24mo.
- Offer a pilot hosted credit equivalent of one month of hosted spend ($12k) to accelerate sign-off; condition: if they convert to Dedicated within 90 days, apply credit to commit.

Architecture / risk notes
- PHI cohort: require VPC + KMS. If they push for on-prem, route to Solutions Eng for sizing; include migration margin in SOW.
- Recommend highlighting caching & batch tuning in the deck — we can often shave 20–40% off the hosted estimate with prefix caching and larger inference batches for offline jobs.

Action items for Wed call
- Diego: walk the assumptions tab and show the break-even chart.
- Steph: prepare a short slide with dedicated pool sizing options (GPUs, throughput targets, burst allowances).
- Marissa: prepare the proposed commercial terms (commit tiers + pilot credit language).
